points.description: States that the learning rate controls the speed of convergence (step size of the steepest descent updates / how fast learning converges).
States that a low learning rate gives slow convergence, described as overdamped.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.25) if only 'slow' is stated without 'overdamped'.

points.description: States that a high learning rate gives underdamped convergence with a zigzagging/oscillating path.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.25) if only zigzag/oscillation is stated without 'underdamped'.

points.description: States the danger: if the learning rate exceeds a critical value, learning becomes unstable (diverges).
points.partial_credit: Half (0.25) if instability/divergence is stated without reference to a critical value or threshold.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all four elements stated explicitly: role in convergence speed, low rate = slow/overdamped, high rate = underdamped/zigzag, and instability above a critical value. Vague statements such as 'too big is bad' earn nothing. A wrong statement within a point (e.g. low rate causes instability) cancels that point. Part marks only where more than half is stated precisely, as specified per point.
